name: two-unrelated-tasks-one-commit
procedure: investigate a frontend/backend card mismatch, then separately add an eval case for tamtamy

truth.title: assert TOPICS["tamtamy"] stages its walkthrough card

expected_fail: Segments into 1 episode against a ground truth of 2, and the first task is not merely merged — it is deleted. The cut loop is right: it produces 4 episodes, cutting at every prompt. `_absorb_before_commit` then folds all four into the single commit at the end, and `trim_leading_exploration` removes the 13 leading read-only steps, which is the whole of task 1. Recorded so the day absorb learns to stop at an unrelated task, the suite says so.
why: Two genuinely different jobs in one sitting. The first asks which walkthrough cards render blank because `TOPICS` stages a body with no key in the frontend's `toolWalkthroughs.ts` — a consistency bug, investigated and reported, nothing written. The second adds the missing eval case for `tamtamy` and commits it. They share a repo and nothing else: different files, different question, different method. One commit at the end covers only the second.
history: The first live session recorded to assert a negative — that the pipeline declines to merge things that should stay apart. Every earlier fixture asserts a positive. Traced on capture: cut loop 4 episodes -> `_absorb_before_commit` 1 -> `trim_leading_exploration` 24 work steps down to 11. The banked candidate is titled after the commit and reads as a tidy 11-step procedure, which is what makes this worse than the module docstring assumes: it says an under-cut candidate 'is visibly wrong and dies at review', and the trim is what stops it looking wrong. Re-extracted after `_KEEP_INPUT` learned to keep `Read`'s path: on the first pass the four reads carried an empty input, so `_substantive`'s read-feeds-a-write rule could not fire on a real capture at all.
